summary: A metal lantern nobody has built, and the page that explains it. What it waits for first is a number off a caliper.
license_note: MIT covers this card, and the grant clause is in examples/moku-card/LICENSE. NOTICE at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/NOTICE.txt lists what the project cannot grant; nothing here enlarges or narrows it.
origin: Not a fork and not a repository of its own. This is a page-project inside mrdirno/vibe-cards, published on that repo's Pages surface, and its host repo's MIT is inherited by the code around the card rather than chosen for the design. The package was generated somewhere else and handed over as a folder; its README says so plainly, and docs/ is that folder's own paperwork kept verbatim. Two of its self-declarations were later disproved by this project: a card url on a domain that does not resolve, and a QR payload recorded as verified that decodes to nothing.
_note: L0, not L1. L0's clauses hold: this manifest is served at the url the card's chip carries, the page it names carries an account-free wishing well, and the repository has a LICENSE with a real SPDX id. L1 is not claimed on either of its added clauses. docs/EVALS.md is Card Studio's eval record, not this card's, so shipped changes here do not carry an eval meeting section 2. And nobody has built this object, so every dimension on the card is drawing arithmetic rather than a fit someone has measured. Section 3 says L0 when in doubt. examples/moku-card/docs/AUTHORSHIP.md discloses human intent, selections and the AI-generated portions. This file states stable facts about this card only. An earlier version embedded byte counts, grep tallies and claims about what other files currently say; every one of those was falsified by the same commit that published them, including one that had claimed this very url was unreachable — a claim that would have been served inside the successful response to fetching it. A manifest that measures its own repository is false on arrival, so this one states no measurement at all.
